title: Single root cover splits invertible-order torsors near a regular divisor
statement: Let i:U→L be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], G a finite group, and W→U a finite etale G-torsor [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. Let R be a commutative regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], φ:Spec R→L, and f∈R a nonzerodivisor with regular quotient R/(f). Suppose |G| is a unit in R. Let β:U×_L Spec R≅D(f) [def-pc-fibre-product] commute with the projections to Spec R. For every y∈Spec R there exist a commutative ring S, a ring map a:R→S, and z∈Spec S such that ψ=Spec(a) is etale and ψ(z)=y. Put g=a(f). There is a positive integer n that is a unit in S, with S and S/(g) regular and g a nonzerodivisor. Put A=S[T]/(T^n-g), N=Spec A, q:N→Spec S its structure map, V=D(g)⊂N, and p:W×_L Spec S→Spec S the projection (using W→L and ψ;φ). There exist d≥0 and an isomorphism δ:(W×_L Spec S)×_{Spec S}V≅⨿_{Fin d}V over V: δ followed by the fold map to V equals the second projection. All rings and schemes are in universe u and G in u+1. This is a splitting by one root extension; no classification into different root exponents is asserted.

proof.text: Pull back the torsor and identify its base with D(f) by beta. The divisor generic-point local rings are DVRs. Generic connected components are Galois under stabilizers in G. By 09EB their ramification and residue degrees divide |G|, so the ramification is tame and the residue extensions separable.

At y on the divisor, pass to the strict henselization. The nonzerodivisor and regular quotient persist. Take n=|G|, positive and a unit. After strict henselization the cover is still a G-torsor; apply the same stabilizer and DVR argument to see that every new ramification index divides n. The n-th root ring is regular local and strictly henselian. By 0BRM the pulled-back torsor is unramified along the root divisor; 0EYE extends it to a finite etale cover of the root ring, which splits over the strictly henselian ring. Restrict to the punctured root cover to get the splitting over V.

The splitting, its inverse and projection identities descend to an affine pointed etale neighborhood by the finite presentation argument of 0EYG (0BSK, 05N9). Take g=a(f). Etale ascent preserves regularity of the base and divisor, and flatness preserves its equation. Off the divisor split the finite etale cover first and use n=1; a(f) is then a unit. Zero splitting factors and empty bases are allowed.

theorem GaloisCover.regular_divisor_root_splitting
    {L U : Scheme.{u}} (i : U ⟶ L)
    (G : Type (u + 1)) [Group G] [Finite G] (W : GaloisCover G U)
    (R : CommRingCat.{u}) (φ : Spec R ⟶ L) (f : R)
    (hG : IsUnit (Nat.card G : R))
    [IsRegularRing R] (hf : IsSMulRegular R f)
    [IsRegularRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span {f})]
    (β : pullback i φ ≅ Scheme.Opens.toScheme (X := Spec R) (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f))
    (hβ : β.hom ≫ Scheme.Opens.ι (X := Spec R) (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f) = pullback.snd i φ)
    (y : Spec R) :
    ∃ (S : CommRingCat.{u}) (a : R ⟶ S) (z : Spec S),
      Etale (Spec.map a) ∧ (Spec.map a) z = y ∧
      let g := a.hom f
      ∃ (n : ℕ),
        (0 < n ∧ IsUnit (n : S)) ∧
        IsRegularRing S ∧ IsSMulRegular S g ∧
        IsRegularRing (S ⧸ Ideal.span {g}) ∧
        let p := pullback.snd (W.π ≫ i) (Spec.map a ≫ φ)
        let A := AdjoinRoot ((Polynomial.X : Polynomial S) ^ n - Polynomial.C g)
        let N := Spec (CommRingCat.of A)
        let q := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap S A))
        let V : N.Opens := PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (algebraMap S A g)
        ∃ (d : ℕ) (δ : pullback p (V.ι ≫ q) ≅ ∐ fun _ : Fin d ↦ V.toScheme),
          δ.hom ≫ Sigma.desc (fun _ : Fin d ↦ 𝟙 V.toScheme) =
            pullback.snd p (V.ι ≫ q)
